scope: Crumb round9; provisional sampled reviews, no universal human-realism ranking

patterns.prompt: One six-second candid phone-camera take, landscape. A fictional woman aged 36 with medium-brown skin, a short uneven dark bob, small freckles and visible under-eye texture, wearing a washed brick-red cotton shirt, sits at a modest cream kitchen table. A plain folded brown bakery bag rests on the table at screen right. Window daylight from camera left, neutral exposure, ordinary phone optics, static eye-level medium close-up. She looks into the lens and says conversationally in English: "I preorder my croissants on Crumb. Breakfast is waiting for me." Her forearms rest on the table; one small glance toward the bag after the last word, then a quiet closed-mouth smile. Natural blink, subtle cheek motion, fine flyaway hairs. No beauty filter, no exaggerated eyebrow lift, no pointing, no product handling, no camera move, no cut, no text or logos. Voice and soft room tone only.
patterns.finding: Correct two-sentence script, stable kitchen/bag and resting hands in samples. Broad eyebrow and head-angle changes; 1.44s transcript gap slows pacing. Face is comparatively smooth. New T2V identity; no cross-shot test.
patterns.hypothesis: Fresh text-only people with one conversational intention and grounded lighting. Same prompt across models; identities are independently generated, so this screens acting and speech rather than controlled identity transfer.

patterns.prompt: One six-second observational bakery interview. A fictional woman baker aged 48, olive skin with uneven pores and smile lines, dark hair loosely tied back with gray strands, in a flour-dusted indigo apron over an oatmeal shirt, sits beside a wooden workbench in a small cream-tiled bakery. Window daylight from camera left, camera locked at eye level, chest-up, hands resting below frame. Her gaze rests on a single interviewer just camera-right. Matter-of-fact, reflective voice in English, beginning promptly: "Crumb puts our bakery preorders in one list. We bake what is booked." After speaking she closes her lips and quietly listens, shoulders settled. Tiny natural eye movements and occasional blink; expression is attentive, no performed enthusiasm. Ordinary documentary lens and unretouched facial texture. No shrugging, head bobbing, broad smiles, music, text, logos or cuts.
patterns.finding: Local transcript contains extra instruction-like speech after the intended line: delivery is steady and unmodulated. Sampled performance is expressive. Reject rather than cut around a prompt-leak failure without listening. The returned expanded prompt is retained in the ledger.
patterns.hypothesis: Fresh text-only people with one conversational intention and grounded lighting. Same prompt across models; identities are independently generated, so this screens acting and speech rather than controlled identity transfer.

patterns.prompt: A six-second ordinary bakery interview, fixed eye-level medium close-up. A fictional 48-year-old woman with olive skin and loosely tied dark hair wears a plain indigo apron and oatmeal shirt. She sits beside a workbench in a cream-tiled neighborhood bakery. Broad soft window daylight from the left, low contrast, ordinary documentary photography. She calmly explains tomorrow’s plan to a colleague beside the camera, with a steady gaze, relaxed brow and resting shoulders. She says once: "Crumb puts our bakery preorders in one list. We bake what is booked." Small conversational mouth movements, a natural blink, then lips close and she listens. Hands rest below the frame. Voice and room tone, no music, no captions, no camera movement.
patterns.finding: Revised prompt yields a much more ordinary face than its first condition, preserved apron and stable bench/window in samples. Speech completes at 5.84s, lips settle by reviewed 6.2s. Eyebrow activity and smooth skin remain. Selected as an affordable calm interview candidate and source of the new return reference; this is a new identity, not proof of causal improvement.
patterns.hypothesis: Both first-round models exaggerated the requested pores/lines and expressions. Remove texture adjectives and long negative list; use broad soft light and one calm communicative intention. Same seed per endpoint, but new text-only output is not an identity-controlled comparison.

patterns.prompt: One continuous five-second editorial bakery product shot. A single freshly baked golden croissant with irregular crisp laminated layers rests on ivory parchment on a round matte cream plate, on a dark walnut bakery counter. The croissant and plate sit in the right half of the image, warm cream tiled background, empty walnut counter at left. Soft morning window light from upper left, physically coherent crumbs and soft shadows, warm neutral white balance. The camera moves slowly straight forward a few centimeters, then eases to a full stop by four seconds and holds the exact final composition. The croissant and plate never move. Real baked pastry texture, understated food photography. No steam, no hands, no extra pastries, no morphing, no lettering, no logos, no cuts.
patterns.finding: Fresh coherent croissant, parchment and plate. Push-in is stronger than the requested few centimeters, but remains one camera direction with stable food. Reviewed 4.5s exit supplies both continuation conditions. Natural food texture; not a real product fidelity benchmark.
patterns.hypothesis: One slow camera movement, static irregular food geometry, and settled exit prepare a fresh continuity reference.

patterns.prompt: Continue this exact photographed bakery pastry shot. The croissant, plate, parchment, crumbs, counter and tiled wall stay stationary in exactly the supplied layout. Locked camera, same crop, same soft left window light and exposure throughout. Hold the settled composition while tiny natural ambient reflections remain plausible. Begin and end on the supplied identical frame. No zoom, rotation, new objects, steam, text, people, music or speech.
patterns.finding: Stable pastry and tile layout in samples. Actual previous-frame to entry RGB MAE 4.59/255, with a slight crop/appearance change. Cheap alternative, but Kling gives the closer boundary in this run. Static hold only; not moving-object continuity.
patterns.hypothesis: Use reviewed exit image for both endpoints. Compare H3 Max with historical preferred Kling for sampled stability and actual boundary closeness; this does not test complex motion.
